name: Socket
summary: Socket is a developer-first security platform that analyzes open-source dependencies for malicious behavior and software supply-chain risk before they reach production.
overview: Socket helps engineering teams identify malicious or risky open-source packages before those dependencies enter production. It announced a $60 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation in May 2026, led by Thrive Capital, after earlier seed, Series A, and Series B financings.

company: Socket evaluates open-source dependencies for malicious behavior, vulnerabilities, and other supply-chain risks before code reaches production. Its approach is designed to fit into developer and security workflows rather than rely solely on disclosed vulnerability databases.

The company raised a $60 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation in May 2026, led by Thrive Capital. Socket said the financing brought total funding to $125 million and would support its next phase of growth as AI changes software-development workflows.
intelligence.why_it_matters: The expansion of AI coding tools increases the volume of open-source code flowing into production environments. Socket is a direct private-market bet on the security layer needed to manage that change.

changed.text: Socket announced a $60M Series C at a $1B valuation, led by Thrive Capital.

takeaways: The Series C established a confirmed $1B valuation and $125M total funding figure.
AI-driven development can expand Socket's addressable security workload.
Incumbent competition and enterprise go-to-market execution remain key risks.
